description: Reader windows `reader-<id>` (UI-30, OQ-40-B, DR-140): created Rust-side by `app_open_reader_window`, they exist outside the main window's `windows` list and would have no IPC access at all without a capability. `core:default` is the floor — a window with no matching capability cannot invoke the pdf commands either. The window permissions are the frameless chrome's own controls (UI-07 pattern): the three control buttons and the `start_dragging` call Tauri's drag-region script makes on the strip. Nothing else: no dialogs, no `set_size` (DR-122's harness-only grant stays with the main window). The one opener grant is `opener:allow-open-url`, added by SPEC-v0.0.9 DR-303 item 6: the EPUB reader routes an external link in book content to the OS default browser through the opener plugin's `openUrl` (the UI-40 pattern); path opens ("Open in external viewer") stay a library-side action reaching `app_open_document`. Page images travel as command payloads read through the asset protocol, whose scope covers `$APPDATA/reader/**` (tauri.conf.json) — the reader cache directory, mirroring the covers pattern (DR-44); EPUB content arrives through the `pdfkeeper-epub` protocol (§3.10), which needs no capability. `updater:default` joins by SPEC-v0.0.10 DR-344: every reader window's chrome carries the settings menu with the *Check for updates* item (UI-50 as revised by DR-338 and DR-344), and the plugin's commands are capability-gated per webview window — without this grant the item exists but cannot run there (the gap DR-329 item 5 predates the menu's move to the chrome).
